output.brief: What is going on: the main driver appears to be the 12 August relay server change. The rebuild imported only 3 of 14 forwarding rules; the old 15-second SpO2 hold-off, 60-second repeat suppression and routing of technical alarms to the charge phone were lost. Phone notifications per nurse roughly doubled in Pods A-C only, and delayed responses rose there for core, agency and new nurses alike. Pod D still uses the old server and did not change. Staffing, acuity and the monitor update do not explain the pattern: alarm volume per patient-day was flat, and Pod D's agency share was similar. Confidence is moderate to high on the relay cause, lower on the exact mechanism and on sick leave. Next: restore the full rule set on the relay server with clinical engineering validation and alarm committee sign-off, then track notifications and acknowledgement times. Do not discipline nurses or cap agency use on this evidence. Do not switch off SpO2 or technical alarm forwarding.
